items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: And I used to like that, Art VanDamne and all those cats. I used to dig the sound.

ctx.x: When did you start making a connection between the solos you were learning by ear and playing so well — the connection with the harmonies that were going on underneath.

Wow. I’d say sometime in high school. Maybe sophomore year, somewhere around there. There was a point where I was playing with an accordion trio. We were playing a lot of weddings and that kind of thing. The guy played chordovox, the organ type accordion, but before that regular accordion. And I used to like that, Art VanDamne and all those cats. I used to dig the sound. There was a fullness to it that I liked. So in any event, we were doing all these weddings and what we would do it get together on Thursdays,…

single tune, just go through the A’s and the B’s and the C’s and the D’s, and then go back and start over again. Week after week. So that when we went to a job we could interpret these tunes that we didn’t know when somebody asked for them. So we could make them sound like something. And also, feeding the computer tunes. Inadvertently, by feeding the computer tunes you are also feeding it changes and finding out, oh, that’s the same as this. Oh, that’s the same as this. Oh that’s the same as this. Oh, that will…
